day.text: The operators open the device room, count the phones, check every battery and login, and hand each phone to its wearer.
Recording runs from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. The operator restarts every phone every 30 minutes.
At every restart the operator looks at what was just recorded and fixes problems on the spot.
Every phone comes back by device number, is inspected, and is counted.
The Portfolio Manager reviews every phone, deletes what must not go out, counts videos and hours per phone and operator, and sends the daily report to Mano.
Anyone who cannot make tomorrow's shift has called and messaged their Portfolio Manager by now.

day.what: The phones are at the hub
day.text: The runner takes all of the site's phones to the closest hub in one trip. They upload and charge there through the night.
The runner brings the phones back to the device room before the operators clock in. The quality control team reviews the footage the next day.

rhythm: Friday is the day off in Egypt. Hotels keep running on Friday on their own wireless internet.
Thursday is the day before the day off. Every phone is flushed on Thursday, and factory phones go to a hub for the night.
Once a week the Portfolio Manager compares the registry, the MDM, and the phones in the device room. Any difference is checked the same day.
Once a week each Portfolio Manager's book is compared with its target.
In the last week of the month Youssef Medhat runs the audit. Footage with a flag is deleted.
After the audit we send the invoice for the accepted hours only. Everyone is paid on that same number.
always: If you cannot come tomorrow, call and message your Portfolio Manager by 8 PM tonight. If you do not, it counts as a no-show.
Each person has one account. Never share your account. Never use an old account again.
Three flags and the worker comes off the phone. A second strike from the client pauses the phone until the worker is trained again.
Never say the client's name to anyone, for any reason.

phases.title: Morning: the phones go out
phases.note: Clock-in is at 7:00 AM. The phones are back from the hub and on the chargers in the device room.

phases.title: During the shift
phases.note: Recording runs from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM. The operator restarts every phone every 30 minutes and checks the footage.

phases.title: Shift end: the phones come back
phases.note: The shift ends at 4:00 PM. Every phone comes back, and the Portfolio Manager reviews the day.

phases.title: Overnight
phases.note: The runner takes the phones to the hub. They upload and charge there through the night. Time passes.

phases.title: The day begins again
phases.note: The runner brings the phones back before 7:00 AM, and the operators start from step 1.

steps.title: Open the device room
steps.done: The room is open at 7:00 AM and every phone is on its charger.
lines: The runner brought the phones back from the hub before 7:00 AM and signed them over to you. Check the number on the phone list.
Nobody records on a phone that has not been counted and checked.

steps.title: Count the phones and write down the number
steps.done: The number you wrote on the count sheet is the number the site should have. If it is not, the Portfolio Manager already knows.
lines: Count by device number, spares included. Write the number and the time on the count sheet.
A phone missing at 7:00 AM goes to the Portfolio Manager now, not at the end of the shift.

steps.title: Check every battery and login
steps.done: Every phone that goes out is charged and logged into its wearer's own account.
lines: A phone that is not charged does not go out. Put it on charge and give the wearer a spare.
One account per person, in their own name. A phone on the wrong account does not go out.

steps.title: Check how much is still uploading
steps.done: Every phone that goes out has room for a full day. Some of last night's footage may still be waiting, and that is fine.
lines: Look at the dashboard. A few videos from last night still waiting is fine. They finish tonight.
A phone that is nearly full stays on charge, and the Portfolio Manager hears before 8:00 AM.

steps.title: Put the phone on the wearer and check it
steps.done: Every phone is on the right head, on the right account, with a clean angle, by 8:00 AM.
lines: Give each wearer their own phone and write it in the wearer log.
Cap on, mount tight, phone in. Set the angle so the camera sees the hands and the work, not the ceiling or the floor.
Say it every day: hat off means tap stop first.

steps.title: Start recording at 8:00 AM
steps.who: The wearer, watched by the operator
steps.done: Every phone on the floor is recording by 8:00 AM with a clean angle.
lines: At 8:00 AM the wearer taps start and begins the assigned task. Not before.
The operator checks the angle and that the phone is recording, then moves to the next one.

steps.title: Restart and check every 30 minutes
steps.done: Every phone restarts on time, and a bad recording is fixed before the next one.
lines: At the buzz, restart every phone that did not restart by itself.
Look at what each phone just recorded: the angle, the light, the wearer working. Fix problems on the spot.
Swap a failing phone for a charged spare and write the swap in the wearer log.

steps.title: What if something goes wrong?
lines: A phone stops working: the wearer gets a charged spare the same minute. Write the swap in the wearer log and tell the Portfolio Manager.
A wearer is not on their own account: they do not film until they are. Tell the Portfolio Manager now.
A wearer takes the rig off without tapping stop: stop the phone, tell them again, and write it down. Twice is a flag.
Someone looks under 18 or has no ID: no phone goes on them. If one is on, take it off. Tell the Portfolio Manager now.
A phone is missing: count again, check the wearer log, then call the Portfolio Manager now.
Someone is hurt: help the person first, then call the Portfolio Manager. If you think it is an incident, it is.

steps.title: The Portfolio Manager or the quality control team visits
steps.who: The Portfolio Manager and the quality control team
steps.done: The site has been seen today at a time nobody expected.
lines: They come without warning, at different times each day.
They check the angles, the restarts, the charging, who has which phone, and how the wearers are doing.

steps.title: Collect every phone at 4:00 PM
steps.done: Every phone that went out this morning is back, by device number.
lines: The wearer taps stop first, then takes the hat off, and brings the whole rig to you.
Tick each phone off the wearer log as it comes back.

steps.title: Inspect and count again
steps.who: The operators, checked by the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: The count matches the morning number, and every damaged phone is written down.
lines: Screen, port, mount, battery. Note any damage next to the device number.
The count must match the morning number. A phone short is a phone missing, and that call happens before anyone goes home.

steps.title: The Portfolio Manager reviews the day
steps.done: Every phone is reviewed, the bad footage is deleted, and the day's hours are written down per phone and per operator.
lines: Go through every phone and everything it recorded today, before any of it uploads.
Delete anything that must not go out: a restroom, a screen, an ID, a person under 18, or a bad recording.
Count the videos and the hours on each phone. Write down how many hours each operator delivered.
Send the daily report to Mano by 6:00 PM: hours, active phones, hardware, problems, fixes.

steps.title: Pack the phones for the runner
steps.who: The operators, the runner, and the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: All of the site's phones are in the bag, counted, and signed for by both sides.
lines: All of the site's phones go in the provided bag. Nothing is written on the outside.
The Portfolio Manager and the runner count the phones together and both sign the phone list.

steps.title: Drive straight to the closest hub
steps.done: The phones are at the hub before 10:00 PM.
lines: Never stop on the way. Never take the phones home.
Keep the company letter and the phone list in the bag. At a checkpoint, show them, stay calm, and call Moharam.

steps.title: At the hub: count, sign, and charge
steps.done: Every phone on the list is counted, signed for, and on a charger.
lines: Count the phones against the phone list and sign it.
Put every phone on a charger and start the upload.

steps.title: Upload overnight and confirm on the dashboard
steps.done: Most of the footage has uploaded before 7:00 AM. The quality control team reviews it the next day.
lines: The phones upload over fiber through the night. What is still waiting in the morning finishes tonight.
The next day, two reviewers watch every video on their own. If either says delete, it is deleted.

steps.title: Back in the device room before 7:00 AM
steps.who: The runner, received by the senior operator
steps.done: Every phone is on its charger in the device room, counted and signed for, before clock-in.
lines: The runner brings the phones back in the same bag. The senior operator counts them against the phone list and both sign.
The operators never wait for the phones.

steps.title: The day begins again
steps.who: The operators, then the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: It is 7:00 AM and step 1 starts again.
lines: Open the room, count the phones, check the batteries and logins, and put the phones on the wearers.

where.s: The phones are at the site, in the device room, and on the wearers.
The phones are at the hub. They upload and charge there.
The runner carries them both ways. Every handover is counted and signed on the phone list.
